findings.title: Claude cost roughly doubled: transcript lines for the same API response are summed with no message.id+requestId dedup
findings.evidence: scan() adds every line that has usage and role=assistant (L210-211) via CostAggregator.add (L261-262). Nothing keys on message.id or requestId. Claude Code writes one JSONL line per content block (thinking/text/tool_use) of a single response, and each line repeats the usage object of that response. Resumed sessions also copy lines across files. Measured on ~/.claude/projects of this machine over the last 7 days (counts only): 65,516 usage lines vs 34,404 unique (message.id, requestId). cache_read 16.55B summed vs 8.88B deduped (1.86x), cache_creation 350.8M vs 168.9M (2.08x), output 40.1M vs 28.2M (1.42x). 16 keys appear in more than one file.
findings.impact: Claude today and 7-day USD in the cost footer and analytics run at about 1.9x the real cost.
findings.fix: Keep a Set of message.id:requestId for the whole estimate() pass, shared across files, and skip keys already seen. When one key appears on several lines, keep the line with the largest output_tokens (16,831 duplicates here carry differing usage). Memo entries must carry their per-file key set so a memo replay cannot count a cross-file duplicate again.
findings.failure_scenario: Two lines carry the same message.id=msg_X and requestId=req_Y and the same usage cache_read_input_tokens=100000, with model claude-opus-5-5. The scanner books 200k cache-read tokens (0.04 USD) where 100k (0.02 USD) is correct.
findings.cetico_evidence: Sources/AiTaskbarCore/Cost/ClaudeSessionScanner.swift:210-262 adds every assistant+usage line. There is no dedup anywhere: grep for requestId/message.id/dedup/seen in Sources/AiTaskbarCore/Cost finds nothing, and the aggregator and memo (L82-87, L102-107) only sum. I re-measured on ~/.claude/projects over 7 days, counts only: 67,539 usage lines vs 35,460 unique (message.id, requestId). 14,527 duplicates carry identical usage; 17,552 differ, mostly output_tokens. Every line had both keys. 16 keys appear in more than one file. Summed vs deduped (keeping max output): cache_read 16.72B vs 8.97B (1.87x), cache_creation 360.6M vs 174.2M (2.07x), output 41.0M vs 29.0M (1.41x). This feeds the cost footer and analytics.

findings.title: Analytics adds OpenAI dollars from opencode into the Codex cost estimate, which CLAUDE.md forbids
findings.evidence: L86 iterates costEstimator.opencode, prices each scan with PricingTable and, when dict[v] already exists (always true for .openai), merges usdToday: existing.usdToday + sumToday and usdLast7Days: existing.usdLast7Days + sumLast7 (L137-138). opencodeProviders maps .openai to [openai]. CLAUDE.md says opencode usage is never merged into the vendor totals: OpenAI traffic rides a subscription (zero marginal cost, so tokens are shown and dollars are not).
findings.impact: The OpenAI analytics card, its donut share and the global total gain list-price dollars for subscription traffic.
findings.fix: Do not merge opencode dollars for subscription-billed vendors (.openai). Keep opencode as a separate token-only breakdown that is excluded from usdToday/usdLast7Days and totalCostUSD.
findings.failure_scenario: The Codex scan gives 12 USD for 7 days and opencode has 1M gpt-5.6-sol input tokens. The OpenAI card shows 16 USD instead of 12.
findings.cetico_evidence: AnalyticsStore.swift:86-146: for every (v, scan) in costEstimator.opencode it prices tokens with PricingTable (L93-94, L105-106). When dict[v] exists, which is always true for .openai because byVendor[.openai] is set at CostEstimator.swift:139, it adds them in at L137-138. CostEstimator.swift:44-45 maps .openai to ["openai"]. The documented decision is in CostEstimator.swift:26-32 itself ('Deliberately NOT merged into byVendor… ~$2.4k/week of notional spend… tokens are shown; the dollars are not') and in CLAUDE.md. Side note, not part of this finding: .zai and .gemini opencode dollars are also added, while .xai is safe because L178 uses max().

findings.title: The monthly analytics timeframe shows the 7-day cost
findings.evidence: case .weekly, .monthly: cost = estimate?.usdLast7Days ?? estimate?.usdToday ?? 0 (and the 7-day model breakdown). For .monthly, currentDuration is 30*86_400 (L86), but no estimate carries 30-day money.
findings.impact: Monthly shows the weekly USD, often about 4x too low. Shares and deltas are then computed against mismatched windows.
findings.fix: Add a 30-day window to CostEstimate (usdLast30Days) from the scanners, or hide cost in .monthly. Never reuse usdLast7Days.
findings.failure_scenario: At a steady 10 USD/day, Weekly shows ~70-80 USD, and Monthly still shows ~70-80 instead of ~300.

test_red_green.name: monthlyTimeframeDoesNotReuseWeeklyCost
test_red_green.assert_after: monthly cost hidden or a 30-day figure

findings.cetico_evidence: AnalyticsAggregator.swift:113-115: `case .weekly, .monthly: cost = estimate?.usdLast7Days`, while currentDuration for .monthly is 30*86400 (L85-86). CostEstimate has no 30-day field. The picker labels it 'Month' (Localizable.strings:326) and totalCostUSD and shares come from it. Downgraded from HIGH: the wrong number only appears in the secondary Analytics view, with no crash, data loss or effect on the main footer.

findings.title: OpenRouter 30-day activity and xAI billing-cycle spend are stored as usdLast7Days
findings.evidence: L166 usdLast7Days: totalFromModels sums OpenRouterActivityItem.usage. OpenRouterWireTypes.swift:66 documents /api/v1/activity as the last 30 days. At L173-177 the xAI invoice-preview cycle spend (spentUSD + prepaidUsedUSD) also goes into usdLast7Days.
findings.impact: The weekly analytics USD for OpenRouter and xAI is a 30-day or cycle-to-date figure, and every vendor share is skewed.
findings.fix: Decode the date of each activity item and sum only the last 7 days. Show xAI cycle spend in its own field with a cycle label.
findings.failure_scenario: OpenRouter at 1 USD/day for 30 days: the weekly card shows 30 USD where 7 is correct.
findings.cetico_evidence: AnalyticsStore.swift:161-166 sums topModels.rawUsage into usdLast7Days. topModels comes from /api/v1/activity, which OpenRouterWireTypes.swift:65-66 documents as 30 days, and it is summed with no date filter (L165-169). The xAI cycle spend also lands in usdLast7Days (L173-178).

findings.title: Repeated token_count events (unchanged total_token_usage) are billed again
findings.evidence: Every token_count with a non-empty last_token_usage is recorded (L363-398), and nothing checks whether info.total_token_usage moved. Measured on ~/.codex/sessions over the last 7 days (counts only): 1,451 of 23,495 events had the same total_tokens as the previous event. Summed last_token_usage is 3.041B tokens vs 2.868B from total deltas (~6% over).
findings.impact: Codex today and 7-day USD are overstated by about 6% on real data.
findings.fix: Decode total_token_usage, track the previous total per file, and skip an event whose total did not increase.
findings.failure_scenario: Two consecutive identical token_count lines (last input 10000, total_tokens 50000) book 20,000 input where 10,000 is correct.
findings.cetico_evidence: CodexSessionScanner.swift:363-398 records every token_count with a non-empty last_token_usage and never reads total_token_usage. I re-measured on ~/.codex/sessions over 7 days: 1,459 of 23,996 events repeat the previous total_tokens, and 1,315 of those also repeat an identical last_token_usage. Summed last is 3.091B vs 2.913B from total deltas (+6.1%). total_token_usage never decreased, so the delta signal is reliable.

findings.title: The last-7-days window spans 8 calendar days, and it disagrees with the now-7d window of opencode
findings.evidence: sevenDaysAgo = startOfToday.addingTimeInterval(-7 * 86_400) (same at CodexSessionScanner.swift:94) keeps today plus 7 full prior days. OpencodeScanner.swift:126 uses now-7*86400, and AnalyticsStore sums the two (L138). A fixed 86_400 s also shifts by an hour across DST.
findings.impact: The 7-day USD includes up to one extra day (about +14% at steady spend), and merged totals mix two windows.
findings.fix: Use cal.date(byAdding: .day, value: -6, to: startOfToday) everywhere, opencode included.
findings.failure_scenario: now = Tue 10:00. A turn from last Tue 09:00 (8 calendar days back) is counted by the Claude/Codex scanners but not by opencode.
findings.cetico_evidence: ClaudeSessionScanner.swift:50 and CodexSessionScanner.swift:94 use startOfToday-7*86400, which covers today plus 7 full prior days (up to 8 calendar days). OpencodeScanner.swift:126 uses now-7*86400, and AnalyticsStore.swift:138 adds the two windows together.

findings.title: The N active sessions figure is actually the number of models with input tokens today
findings.evidence: for usage in totals.values where usage.inputTokens > 0 { sessionCount += 1 } iterates totalsByModel, which is the TODAY bucket (ClaudeSessionScanner.swift:146), for every timeframe. VendorAnalyticsCardView.swift:181 renders it as N active sessions.
findings.impact: The session count is wrong everywhere: 12 sessions on one model show as 1 session.
findings.fix: Count distinct transcript or rollout files in the window inside the scanners and expose that count, or drop the label.
findings.failure_scenario: 12 Claude sessions today on claude-opus-5-5 show as 1 session.
findings.cetico_evidence: AnalyticsAggregator.swift:133-136 counts totalsByModel entries with inputTokens>0. totalsByModel is the TODAY bucket (ClaudeSessionScanner.swift:146, CodexSessionScanner.swift:182). VendorAnalyticsCardView.swift:178-181 renders it as 'active sessions'. Downgraded: it is a wrong label on an informational number, and cost is unaffected.

findings.title: Anthropic Usage credits (extra_usage) is folded into windows, so it drives the menu-bar percent and notifications
findings.evidence: .anthropic windows = [s.session, s.weekly] + s.scoped + [s.opus, s.credits]. maxUtilization = windows.max (L71) feeds UsageStore.maxUtilization and history, and NotificationService.observe iterates windows. CLAUDE.md sets this rule for Codex credits: folding them together made the menu bar read 80% from credits while the plan sat at 10%. Anthropic extra_usage is the same kind of monthly overage budget.
findings.impact: A red 92% menu bar and approaching-limit notifications appear while the plan windows sit at 10%.
findings.fix: Exclude credits from windows and render it as a separate row, or at least keep it out of maxUtilization and the notification loop.
findings.failure_scenario: extra_usage.utilization 92 with five_hour 10 and seven_day 12: the menu bar shows 92%.
findings.cetico_evidence: It is true that UsageSnapshot.swift:44-46 puts s.credits in windows and therefore in maxUtilization. The premise that this is 'the same kind' as Codex credits does not hold. Anthropic extra_usage has a server-side denominator (monthly_limit plus utilization, AnthropicWireTypes.swift:176-185), while the CLAUDE.md rule targets Codex's locally derived high-water mark. OpenRouter, Kimi and xAI balances are also in windows by design. Whether an overage budget near its cap should tint the menu bar is a product decision, not a proven defect.

findings.title: A missing remaining_fraction defaults to 1.0, so an exhausted Antigravity bucket can read 0% used
findings.evidence: let rem = bucket.remainingFraction ?? 1.0. The snake_case keys look like proto JSON, and proto3 JSON omits zero-valued fields by default, so remaining_fraction == 0 (fully spent) may arrive as an absent key. I could not confirm this without running agy.
findings.impact: If the key is omitted at 0, a fully spent Gemini bucket shows 0% used / 100% remaining.
findings.fix: Treat a missing fraction as unknown (skip the window or flag it), never as fully available. Add a fixture with no remaining_fraction.
findings.failure_scenario: The bucket {id: gemini-5h, window: 5h, reset_time: ...} has no fraction, and the UI shows Gemini (5h) 0%.
findings.cetico_evidence: GeminiWireTypes.swift:150 defaults to 1.0, and WireTypesEdgeTests.swift:316 pins that as intended. The only real sample (Fixtures.swift:416-443) always emits the key, even at 1.0. The proto3 omit-zero theory is unverified, as the finder admits. Without an observed exhausted-bucket payload there is no proof.

findings.title: History records stale-fallback and cache-hit snapshots as new samples stamped now
findings.evidence: recordHistory runs for every .ok outcome, including CachedFetch fallback outcomes (isStale, up to 7 d old) and fresh-cache replays, and stamps Date.now (L277).
findings.impact: During an outage the sparkline, peak day and deltas keep plotting the pre-outage percent after the window has reset. Manual refreshes also over-weight the averages in AnalyticsAggregator (L145-146).
findings.fix: Record only real network fetches (not stale, cacheAge <= 1), or stamp the sample with outcome.fetchedAt and dedupe on it.
findings.failure_scenario: At 95%, the network drops for 6 h and the window resets. History logs 95% every 5 min.
findings.cetico_evidence: VendorViewModel.swift:235 calls recordHistory for every .ok outcome, including CachedFetch stale fallbacks and fresh-cache replays. It stamps Date.now (L277) and ignores outcome.isStale and fetchedAt, while the same function already knows cacheAge (L231).

findings.title: Grok prepaidUsedUSD is invented as remaining balance x weekly usage percent
findings.evidence: if let pct = cfg.creditUsagePercent, let balance = prepaidUSD, pct > 0 { return (balance * pct) / 100.0 }. creditUsagePercent is the weekly subscription utilization (L261-270) and prepaidBalance is the remaining USD. AnalyticsStore.swift:173 shows the product as xAI spend.
findings.impact: xAI analytics shows fabricated spend whenever onDemandUsed is absent.
findings.fix: Return nil when onDemandUsed is missing.
findings.failure_scenario: Balance 50 USD and weekly 40% produce 20 USD spent where the real figure is 0.
findings.cetico_evidence: XAIWireTypes.swift:286-291: when onDemandUsed is absent, prepaidUsedUSD = prepaidBalance * creditUsagePercent/100. creditUsagePercent is the weekly subscription utilization (L261) and prepaidBalance is the remaining balance, so the product has no meaning. AnalyticsStore.swift:173 displays it as spend.

findings.title: Pre-release suffixes compare lexicographically, so beta10 < beta9
findings.evidence: case let (sa?, sb?): return sa > sb is a String comparison, so beta10 > beta9 is false.
findings.fix: Split identifiers on dots and numeric runs, then compare the numeric parts as integers per SemVer section 11.
findings.cetico_evidence: Semver.swift:24 compares suffixes as Strings, so isNewer("0.24.0-beta10", than: "0.24.0-beta9") is false. In production today this is unreachable: fetchLatest uses /releases/latest (UpdateChecker.swift:150), which never returns a prerelease, and release.yml marks every '-' tag as prerelease, so two prerelease versions are never compared. No '-' tags exist. Downgraded to INFO; it becomes LOW as soon as BUG-ART-014 is fixed.

findings.title: An opencode scan failure (nil) is published as no data and erases the previous rows
findings.evidence: OpencodeScanner.scan(providerGroups:) ?? [:]. Any non-DONE step (SQLITE_BUSY while opencode writes, or a prepare failure after a schema change) returns nil, which becomes [:] and is assigned to self.opencode (L173).
findings.impact: The opencode rows flicker away on a transient lock, and schema drift looks like no usage.
findings.fix: Keep the Optional through: on nil, keep the previous value and log.
findings.failure_scenario: opencode holds a write lock during a refresh, so the scan returns nil and the Models section loses its opencode rows.
findings.cetico_evidence: CostEstimator.swift:73 turns a nil scan into [:], and L165-173 publishes it, wiping the previous opencode rows. OpencodeScanner returns nil on open, prepare or non-DONE step (L111, L155, L211). The SQLITE_BUSY vector is weak: opencode's DB is a WAL reader, and there is no busy_timeout. Schema drift or a prepare failure clearly triggers it.

findings.title: include_prereleases can never take effect: /releases/latest never returns pre-releases
findings.evidence: fetchLatest() uses GET /repos/{repo}/releases/latest (L150). The releases API documents that endpoint as the latest full release, excluding drafts and pre-releases. raw.prerelease is always false, so the includePrereleases branch is dead.
findings.impact: Users who opt in to betas are never offered one.
findings.fix: When the flag is set, query /releases?per_page=10, drop drafts, and pick the max by Semver.
findings.failure_scenario: v0.24.0-beta1 is published with include_prereleases = true, and the checker still says up to date.
findings.cetico_evidence: UpdateChecker.swift:150 queries only /releases/latest, which GitHub defines as the latest non-draft, non-prerelease release. The includePrereleases branch at L167 therefore never sees raw.prerelease == true and is dead.
